title: Evening QA mismatch: deployment scrub and on-call notes
content:
Summary:

Evening QA mismatch observed after staged deployment of model-variant v2q-dec (a quantized variant of customer-chat-3). Canary nodes returned responses that diverged semantically for longer prompts (>320 tokens) compared to baseline. The discrepancy was first noticed by the QA team running routine end-to-end conversational scripts that include long context windows. Short prompt sampling that our canary monitoring relies on did not surface the issue.

Impact:
- A subset of traffic routed through the new variant returned truncated/garbled continuations for prompts containing nested code blocks or lengthy enumerations.
- Estimated affected requests: ~0.4% of total requests served by the staging region between 2025-03-04 19:12 and rollback at 2025-03-05 02:04 UTC.
- No production customer reported data loss, but internal QA found reproducible quality regressions on our evaluation harness (bleu-like and token-levenshtein metrics degraded).

How it was discovered:
- 2025-03-04 18:58 UTC: QA run triggered nightly long-context suite against the new variant in the staging cluster.
- 2025-03-04 19:08 UTC: Automated diff job flagged >20% per-prompt token distribution mismatch for tests longer than 320 tokens.
- 2025-03-04 19:12 UTC: QA engineer Mei opened SRE-1124 and pinged #oncall.

Immediate timeline (high level):
- 19:12 UTC: First alert from QA harness (Mei).
- 19:18 UTC: On-call (Priya) acknowledged and started preliminary checks (health, pod logs, checksum comparisons).
- 19:30 UTC: Observed that canary sampling in monitoring dashboards used mostly short prompts (median length 48 tokens) — blind spot.
- 19:45 UTC: Pulled runtime logs from variant pods; saw a higher-than-expected number of tokenization warnings ("unknown-subtoken-map") originating from the tokenizer shim.
- 20:05 UTC: Ran local inference with the same model artifact and a curated 600-token prompt; reproduced truncated continuation.
- 20:40 UTC: Rolled canary percentage to 0% for the new variant in the staging rollout config (manual traffic cut).
- 21:10 UTC: Began controlled rollback of v2q-dec to previous stable variant on staging. Rollback completed by 22:06 UTC.
- 23:20 UTC: Notified product and release owners. Began root cause analysis.
- 2025-03-05 02:04 UTC: Clean production check and final verification done. Deployment blocked until further checks added.

Initial findings / hypothesis:
1) Tokenizer-mapping divergence: The quantized build pipeline introduced a tokenizer adapter bump (v1.4.7 -> v1.5.0) that changed fallback behavior for unknown subtoken sequences. The new adapter emits a warning and substitutes an alias token sequence which, when combined with the quantized decoder's beam truncation heuristic, caused early EOS-like signals for long nested segments.
2) Canary sampling bias: Our canary monitors sample primarily short queries. Because the failure mode only appears on >320-token contexts, automated canary checks did not trigger.
3) Kernel scheduling sensitivity: Secondary hypothesis — the quantized execution path slightly changes per-token latency distribution which interacts with our microbatch allocator and leads to earlier token emission under certain memory pressure patterns. Logs show increased microbatch retries around the time of observed failures.

Mitigations taken (immediate):
- Stopped further rollouts of v2q-dec.
- Reduced canary traffic to 0% and rolled back staging to the last stable variant.
- Isolated the tokenizer adapter change in the CI artifact chain and reproduced locally with both adapter versions to confirm behavioral delta.
- Added a temporary canary test that runs a small suite of long-context prompts (320–1024 tokens) against every variant promotion pipeline.

Reproduction notes (how QA reproduced):
- Test harness used: internal/eval/long-context-suite v3.2 (script attached in the linked PR).
- Example failing prompt (sanitized): multi-part instruction with three nested code blocks and long numbered lists (>450 tokens).
- Local reproduction command: ./serve-local --model model-v2q-dec --prompt-file long_context_case_07.txt --max-tokens 512 --kv-cache-enabled
- Observed output: abrupt stop at ~280 tokens with trailing replacement token sequences; baseline model returns full continuation.

Root cause analysis plan (next steps):
- Confirm token mapping diff: run tokenized dumps for a set of canonical long prompts across the two tokenizer adapter versions and compute per-token mapping diffs. Owner: Ethan Morales. ETA: 2025-03-10.
- Quantized runtime trace: capture per-layer token emission timestamps and microbatch allocator logs to see correlation between allocator retries and premature EOS. Owner: Carlos Ruiz. ETA: 2025-03-09.
- End-to-end variant promotion checks: add long-context evaluation stage to the pipeline before canary promotion. Owner: Riya Patel (release-engineering). ETA: 2025-03-12.
- Determine whether to pin tokenizer adapter used by quantized builds to v1.4.7 until runtime integrates safe-fallbacks. Owner: Priya Nambiar. Decision due: 2025-03-11.

Runbook / playbook updates (short-term):
- Add "long-context smoke" to canary monitor suite (automated, must run for every promotion).
- Update the rollout checklist to include a tokenizer-hash checksum comparison step between baseline and variant artifacts.
- Improve runbook steps for microbatch-related regressions: include commands to fetch allocator state and trigger a scaled local replay.

Permanent mitigations (design/infra):
- Instrument tokenizer adapter to expose a token-mismatch metric (per-deployment): counts of unknown-subtoken events and fallback substitutions.
- Add an automated check that fails promotions when the per-token emission distribution deviates beyond threshold for long-context tests.
- Add a synthetic traffic generator that periodically hits staging variants with long, nested prompts to detect regressions early.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Does the alias substitution semantics make sense to keep in the adapter long-term, or should it be made opt-in for quantized models?
- How often do microbatch allocation retries correlate with solver heuristics in quantized builds (we need broader sampling across regions)?
- Were there any staggered regional differences that masked this earlier (we saw staging only; production was not promoted)?

Lessons learned (short bullets):
- Canary sampling diversity is critical: short median prompt length can mask long-context regressions.
- Artifact-level changes (tokenizer adapter) can have outsized effects when combined with runtime heuristics (quantized decoder).
- Nightly QA long-context suites are valuable — promote those tests earlier in the promotion pipeline.

Action items (owners + deadlines):
- Ethan: Produce token-dump diff report between adapters. Due 2025-03-10.
- Carlos: Collect and analyze allocator traces from the failed time window and an unaffected window. Due 2025-03-09.
- Riya: Add long-context stage to promotion pipeline and update docs. Due 2025-03-12.
- Priya: Decide on adapter pin / temporary veto on future quantized promotions until safe-fallback is implemented. Decision by 2025-03-11.
- Mei: Expand nightly QA set with three additional long-context prompts and add to the canary trigger list. Due 2025-03-07.

Appendix A — On-call notes (raw):
- 19:18 UTC (Priya): checked pod liveness and restart frequency — all green.
- 19:25 UTC (Priya): found repeated tokenizer warnings in pod logs (see linked log snippet in PR 1342).
- 19:40 UTC (Ethan): confirmed tokenizer adapter bump present in artifact metadata (build tag: quant-adapter-1.5.0).
- 20:00 UTC (Riya): executed manual traffic cut in rollout controller (set newVariant.percent=0).
- 20:45 UTC (Carlos): performed local reproduce and captured token stream and emitted tokens file for diffing.

Appendix B — Quick checks to run next time (cheat sheet):
- curl /health and /metrics on variant pods; check tokenization warnings counter.
- run sample suite: long_context_case_*.txt against variant with --kv-cache-enabled and --no-cache to compare behavior.
- dump tokenizer hash: ./tools/tokenizer-hash --artifact model-v2q-dec >> tokenizer_hash.txt and compare with baseline.

Notes to self:
- Keep the incident writeup concise when sharing externally; focus on customer impact (none reported) and mitigations.
- Coordinate with model-onboarding to require explicit compatibility notes for tokenizers when changing adapter versions.

End of doc.
